title: The Tractor to the Casa de Pizarro: the Rector, the Autogolpe, and the Cell at Barbadillo
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Lima, a birth on a disputed day
stops.date_confidence: contested. The electoral register and his own promoted biography give 28 July 1938; en.wikipedia and other civil records give 26 July 1938, in Miraflores. A 1997 Caretas investigation alleged birth at Kawachi in Kumamoto on a falsified Peruvian record; Japan's Foreign Ministry inquiry of December 2000 concluded the birth had been registered at its Lima consulate. The contradiction is recorded, not resolved. The parents' joint 1934 passage aboard the Boyoku Maru is [R], dossier synthesis only.
stops.campa: Naoichi Fujimori and Mutsue Inomoto come out of Kumamoto in 1934 and make their living in Lima mending tires and taking in sewing. Their eldest son is born four years later into a colony that speaks Japanese at the table and Spanish at the counter, and that will be expropriated, blacklisted and shipped to camps in the United States while his parents' country loses its war. The day printed on his identity papers is the twenty-eighth of July, which is also the day Peru celebrates its independence. Other records give the twenty-sixth.
suggested_refs: Peruvian RENIEC and electoral-register entries for Alberto Kenya Fujimori Inomoto
The Japanese consular birth registry of Lima, 1938, cited in Japan's December 2000 nationality finding
sources: CIDOB biographical chronology, cited in the research dossier
Caretas (1997) birthplace investigation, reported in en.wikipedia

stops.name: Lima, the Japanese school and the Spanish ones
stops.date_confidence: [R] for the coordinate, which is an approximation for central Lima: Nominatim returns no historic Colegio Nuestra Senora de la Merced at this location, only unrelated schools of that name in Pachacamac and Mirones Bajo. The school sequence is [A] from en.wikipedia (Hoshi Shokai Gakuen 1946-1948, La Rectora 1949, La Merced, then the Gran Unidad Escolar Alfonso Ugarte, leaving 1956); the year of each individual transfer is not separately documented.
stops.campa: The boy is sent first to the Hoshi Shokai Gakuen, a school of the Japanese colony where the lessons are given in his parents' language. Then the family turns him toward Spanish and the Church: La Rectora, then Nuestra Senora de la Merced, then the Gran Unidad Escolar Alfonso Ugarte in Brena. The parents choose that sequence; nobody asks the child. He leaves the Alfonso Ugarte in 1956 with a Peruvian secondary certificate and a household that still speaks Japanese at the table.
suggested_refs: Records of the Japanese-Peruvian community schools of Lima before and after the 1941-1945 expropriations
sources: CIDOB biographical chronology, cited in the research dossier

stops.name: La Molina, first in the class
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives entry to the Universidad Nacional Agraria La Molina and graduation first in his class in 1961. April is the ordinary start of the Peruvian academic year and is a placeholder; no month is given in the sources.
stops.campa: He enters the National Agrarian University at La Molina to read agricultural engineering and comes out of it first in his class in 1961. The campus is a working farm on the eastern edge of the city: canals, test plots, cattle pens, and a faculty that measures a man by yield and by arithmetic. He stays. He teaches mathematics there, then physics, then serves as dean of sciences. No political speech of any kind and no party membership appear in the record of those years. He is on the same university's payroll for close to three decades.
suggested_refs: Universidad Nacional Agraria La Molina faculty and rectorship records, 1962-1989
sources: CIDOB biographical chronology, cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Strasbourg, a year of pure physics
stops.date_confidence: attested for the stay, [R] for the month, which is not given. Coordinate corrected to the Nominatim position of the Universite de Strasbourg on the Boulevard de la Victoire; the dossier's 48.5779, 7.7409 falls about 1.7 km west of the university quarter. es.wikipedia specifies the subject as Fisica Pura. No completed Strasbourg degree is established anywhere in the record.
stops.campa: He crosses to France in 1964 and spends a year at the University of Strasbourg reading what the Spanish sources call Fisica Pura. No degree from the stay is established anywhere in the record. Campaign biographies will later turn the year into a completed European doctorate, and the version holds, repeated by people with no interest in checking it. He comes back to La Molina and goes on teaching mathematics to agronomists. What else the year in Strasbourg gave him, the record does not say.
suggested_refs: Universite de Strasbourg enrolment records for the 1964 academic year

stops.name: Milwaukee, the master's in mathematics
stops.date_confidence: attested by en.wikipedia: Master of Science in mathematics, University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, on a Ford Foundation scholarship, 1969. The month is a placeholder for the academic year's end; no date is given.
stops.campa: A Ford Foundation scholarship takes him to the University of Wisconsin at Milwaukee, where he takes a Master of Science in mathematics in 1969. It is his second foreign university in five years and the last degree the record gives him. Later profiles will move him to Madison, the larger campus, the same way they moved the Strasbourg year into a doctorate. Both errors run in his favour, and neither is ever traced back to him. He goes back to La Molina with the degree and no visible intention of ever leaving teaching. He is thirty-one.
suggested_refs: University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee graduate records, 1969; Ford Foundation Latin American scholarship files

segments.name: The Rector and the Dark Horse

stops.name: Lima, the marriage to Susana Higuchi
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia, 'Susana Higuchi', gives 25 July 1974. Keiko's birth on 25 May 1975 is attested by en.wikipedia, 'Keiko Fujimori'. The separation and removal from the office of First Lady fall in 1994; the divorce was formalised by a Lima tribunal in 1995, and the two years are frequently conflated.
stops.campa: He marries Susana Higuchi Miyagawa on the twenty-fifth of July, 1974, a civil engineer out of the same immigrant generation whose father already knows his. She reads hydraulics, he reads mathematics, and between them they build a small construction company and four children, Keiko first in May of the following year and Kenji last in 1980. The company is theirs jointly and the house is full of children before either of them is forty. The marriage ends twenty years on, in public, inside the government palace, with her accusing his relatives of selling clothing donated from Japan for the poor.
suggested_refs: Peruvian civil marriage register, Lima, 25 July 1974
susana_higuchi.journey.json, 'Lima Centro, the Capilla de la Virgen de la O'

stops.name: La Molina, the rector
stops.date_confidence: attested: rector of the Universidad Nacional Agraria La Molina 1984-1989 and president of Peru's National Assembly of Rectors from 1987 (en.wikipedia). The month is a placeholder; the sources give years only.
stops.campa: He is elected rector of the agrarian university and holds it for five years, and in 1987 the rectors of Peru elect him president of their National Assembly. The country whose small piece of state he now administers is coming apart: inflation past four figures, Sendero Luminoso dropping the pylons that light Lima, the government of Alan Garcia burning through what is left of the reserves. A rectorship is not a political office. Every year of the five he negotiates the university's budget with a treasury holding less than it held the year before.
suggested_refs: Asamblea Nacional de Rectores del Peru, presidency records 1987-1989
sources: CIDOB biographical chronology, cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Santa Beatriz, Concertando on Channel 7
stops.date_confidence: attested that he hosted Concertando on the state channel from 1987; the coordinate is corrected to the IRTP building at Avenida Jose Galvez 1040, Santa Beatriz, Cercado de Lima (Nominatim), not the Jesus Maria pin the dossier carried. The month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: On the state channel, from the IRTP building on Avenida Jose Galvez, he hosts a public-affairs programme called Concertando. It is a modest slot with a modest audience. He interviews ministers of the Garcia government he is quietly measuring, and the camera gives him what the Peruvian political class cannot manufacture for itself in 1987: a face that arrives in living rooms with no party standing behind it. He is still hosting the programme in 1989, the year he registers a party of his own.
suggested_refs: IRTP / Television Nacional del Peru programme archives for Concertando, 1987-1989
sources: CIDOB biographical chronology, cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Lima, Cambio 90 registered
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia, 'Cambio 90', confirms registration on 5 October 1989 and gives the motto as Honradez, Tecnologia, Trabajo. The dossier's 'Honestidad' is a misquote and is not carried here. The coordinate is a general-Lima pin; no registration-office address was located. The quoted poster title is a campaign slogan addressed to the voter, not a first-person utterance by Fujimori.
stops.campa: On the fifth of October 1989 he registers a movement called Cambio 90 under a motto of three words: Honradez, Tecnologia, Trabajo. Its people are small-business owners, provincial schoolteachers, market vendors and the evangelical churches that no Peruvian party has ever bothered to court. It has no money, no machine and no newspaper of its own. The candidate campaigns from the seat of a tractor through the shanty districts, and the posters, printed on newsprint, address the voter in the second person.
stops.quote: Alberto Fujimori: Un presidente como tu
stops.quote_source: Title of the 1990 Cambio 90 campaign poster, Sam L. Slick Collection, University of New Mexico, and of the 1990 campaign spot held in the PUCP audiovisual archive
suggested_refs: The 1990 newsprint poster in the Sam L. Slick Collection, shelfmark ZIM CSWR Pict Colls PICT 000-674-3687, Drawer 30 Folder 5
sources: Sam L. Slick Collection of Latin American and Iberian Posters, Center for Southwest Research, University of New Mexico, item 'Alberto Fujimori: Un presidente como tu' (1990)
PUCP audiovisual archive, 1990 campaign spot 'Un presidente como tu'

stops.name: Lima, the first round and the runoff
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia, '1990 Peruvian general election', gives the runoff on 10 June 1990 with 4,489,897 votes, 62.38 per cent, against 37.62 for Vargas Llosa. The dossier collapsed the runoff into 28 July, which is the inauguration; the two are separated here. The first-round figure of about 29 per cent is [R], dossier synthesis.
stops.campa: In April he takes about twenty-nine per cent and finishes second, which no poll predicted, behind the novelist Mario Vargas Llosa and the coalition of the established Lima parties standing behind him. Between the rounds the country works out what it is choosing between: a novelist who has published his shock programme in advance, and a university rector nobody can place. On the tenth of June the runoff returns 4,489,897 votes for Fujimori, 62.38 per cent, against 37.62 for the novelist.
suggested_refs: Jurado Nacional de Elecciones returns for the second round of 10 June 1990

stops.name: United Nations Headquarters, the creditors in one room
stops.date_confidence: attested in the dossier's chronology (line 87) for the 29 June 1990 meeting convened by Perez de Cuellar with Camdessus, Conable and Iglesias, and for the Miami stop on the return leg; not independently re-fetched in this pass. The Miami consultation is folded into this stop rather than given a pin of its own.
stops.campa: Before he takes office he flies to New York, where the Secretary-General, Javier Perez de Cuellar, a Peruvian, puts him in a room with Michel Camdessus of the Fund, Barber Conable of the World Bank and Enrique Iglesias of the Inter-American Development Bank. Peru is in arrears and outside the credit system altogether. On the way home, in Miami, economists including Carlos Rodriguez Pastor and Carlos Bolona argue for one brutal correction rather than the gradual programme his own advisers have drafted. He listens to Miami.
suggested_refs: The gradualist 'seven samurai' programme drafted for the transition and set aside in July 1990
sources: Research dossier line 87 (CIDOB-derived), tagged [A] there but not independently re-fetched

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the oath and the shock
stops.date_confidence: attested for the inauguration on 28 July 1990 and for the announcement of the stabilisation package on 8 August by prime minister Juan Carlos Hurtado Miller; the package itself is [R], dossier synthesis, not re-verified against a primary news account. The coordinate is the canonical Casa de Pizarro pin already used by susana_higuchi, keiko_fujimori and pizarro.
stops.campa: On the twenty-eighth of July he takes the oath in the Casa de Pizarro on the Plaza Mayor and moves his family into the government house. He had spent the campaign telling the shanty districts that no shock would be done to them. Eleven days later his prime minister, Juan Carlos Hurtado Miller, announces the correction on television: price controls lifted, subsidies withdrawn, fuel multiplied several times over in a single night. Bread follows the fuel. The country names it the Fujishock.
suggested_refs: Hurtado Miller's televised address of 8 August 1990 announcing the stabilisation package
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, 'Palacio de Gobierno, the twenty-eighth of July'

stops.name: Barrios Altos, 840 Jiron Huanta
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia, 'Barrios Altos massacre', gives the street address, the date, fifteen dead including an eight-year-old and four wounded. Coordinate corrected to the Nominatim resolution of 840 Jiron Huanta, Barrio Chirimoyo, Barrios Altos; the dossier's pin fell about 2.2 km north of the Rimac, outside the district. The 2009 conviction is [A].
stops.campa: A tenement at 840 Jiron Huanta is holding a neighbourhood barbecue to raise money for repairs when men in hoods come up the stairs with silenced weapons and shoot everyone in the yard. Fifteen die, one of them a boy of eight, and four are left wounded. The killers are a detachment of army intelligence that the courts will eventually name Grupo Colina, and eighteen years later a Peruvian supreme court will convict the president who was in office that night as an indirect perpetrator. The government of the day says nothing about it at all.
suggested_refs: Inter-American Court of Human Rights, Barrios Altos v. Peru (2001), on the amnesty laws
sources: Peruvian Supreme Court judgment of 7 April 2009, as summarised in the research dossier

stops.name: Pativilca, six taken from Barranca
stops.date_confidence: attested in the dossier (lines 111, 304-306) for the 29 January 1992 abduction and killing of six residents by Grupo Colina members, and for the case still being tried against Fujimori at his death; not independently re-fetched. The coordinate approximates the town of Pativilca, not the killing site.
stops.campa: North of Lima, in the sugar country of Barranca province, six residents of Pativilca are taken out of their houses, tortured and killed. It is the same detachment, working the same year, in a province where no journalist is watching and no magazine will be handed a map. The case takes more than three decades to reach a courtroom with Fujimori inside it, and it is still being heard on the day he dies in his daughter's house in September 2024. No verdict was ever entered against him for Pativilca.
suggested_refs: The Pativilca case file before the Sala Penal Especial, open at the defendant's death in 2024
sources: Research dossier lines 111, 304-306, from the Peruvian human-rights prosecutions

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, the troops in the chamber
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia records the self-coup of 5 April 1992, the dissolution of Congress and the intervention of the judiciary; the dossier (lines 104-105) adds the occupation of Congress and of newsrooms. Coordinate is the canonical Palacio Legislativo pin already used by susana_higuchi and keiko_fujimori.
stops.campa: Late on a Sunday night he appears on television and dissolves the Congress of the Republic, suspends the constitution, and announces the intervention of the courts, the public ministry, the constitutional tribunal and the comptroller. Tanks take the Plaza Bolivar. Soldiers occupy the legislative palace and the newsrooms, and opposition politicians are held inside their own houses. He calls it a government of emergency and national reconstruction. Peru calls it the autogolpe, the coup a president carries out against his own state.
stops.quote: Disolver, disolver temporalmente el Congreso de la Republica.
stops.quote_source: Alberto Fujimori, televised address of 5 April 1992, as compiled in es.wikiquote citing Mario Vargas Llosa (2001) p. 46 and Raul Wiener (2001) p. 98; the underlying book pages were not reachable in this pass
suggested_refs: The televised address of 5 April 1992 in full

stops.name: San Borja, the Pentagonito
stops.date_confidence: the date of the self-coup is attested; that the family was moved out of the Casa de Pizarro into the army intelligence installations rests on Susana Higuchi's own later account and was denied by the government, and no court established it. Coordinate inherited byte-for-byte from susana_higuchi.journey.json.
stops.campa: The family is taken out of the Casa de Pizarro that week and lodged, by Susana Higuchi's account, inside the installations of the army intelligence service at San Borja, the concrete star that the city calls the Pentagonito. She says she had in effect already been seized before the tanks moved. The government denied it and no court has established it. The detachment that killed at Barrios Altos was quartered under the same command, and the Cantuta bodies were first said to have passed through this building.
suggested_refs: Servicio de Inteligencia del Ejercito facilities at San Borja, later the subject of criminal proceedings
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, 'Lima, out of the palace after the autogolpe' and 'San Borja, the basements of the SIE'

stops.name: La Cantuta, nine students and a professor
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia, 'La Cantuta massacre', confirms the university, the district and the ten victims including professor Hugo Munoz. Coordinate corrected to the Nominatim position of the Universidad Nacional de Educacion Enrique Guzman y Valle; the dossier's pin fell nine to ten kilometres southwest, in open country. The clandestine burial sites are not separately pinned, since no recoverable place name was reached.
stops.campa: Soldiers enter the education university at Chosica before dawn, put the students face down on the floors of their residence halls, and take away nine of them along with a professor, Hugo Munoz. The ten are killed and buried in secret, then dug up, burned, and buried a second time. A magazine in Lima receives a hand-drawn map to the first graves. In 2009 the supreme court will use this case and Barrios Altos to fix criminal responsibility on the president. Where the remains were put the second time has never been established in a form anyone can point to on a map.
suggested_refs: The Cieneguilla graves and the hand-drawn map published in Lima in 1993
sources: Peruvian Supreme Court judgment of 7 April 2009, as summarised in the research dossier

stops.name: Surquillo, the capture of Abimael Guzman
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia, 'Abimael Guzman', gives 12 September 1992, a house in Surquillo, and the arrest of Guzman with Elena Iparraguirre and two other women. The unit was the GEIN of DIRCOTE under General Ketin Vidal; the dossier's 'DINCOTE' is the directorate's later name and is anachronistic for 1992. The coordinate is district-level; the house address was not verified.
stops.campa: In a rented house above a dance studio in Surquillo, a police intelligence group that has been reading Abimael Guzman's rubbish for months walks in and takes him without a shot fired, together with Elena Iparraguirre and two other women. The Shining Path loses its founder and its archive in one evening. The truth commission that examines the decade records the capture as police work, patient and unarmed, carried out with no instruction from the palace. The president is not there and had not been told in advance. He will campaign on it for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: The GEIN surveillance files on the Surquillo house, 1992
sources: Comision de la Verdad y Reconciliacion, cited in the research dossier lines 115, 371

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, the charter of 1993
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia records the Democratic Constituent Congress elections of 22 November 1992, in which Cambio 90-Nueva Mayoria took 44 of 80 seats, and the approval of the new constitution by referendum at about 52 per cent; promulgation on 29 December 1993 is from the dossier (lines 118-119). The erasure of the signature in the official catalogue of signatories is [A] from en.wikipedia, 'Constitution of Peru'; a reported 2025 congressional vote to restore it could not be confirmed.
stops.campa: The constituent congress elected after the coup, in which his own list holds forty-four of eighty seats, produces a new constitution: a smaller state, a single chamber, private capital written into the articles on mining and water, and a president permitted to stand again. The referendum on the thirty-first of October carries it by about fifty-two per cent, and he promulgates it in December. It outlives his government, his imprisonment and his death. The official catalogue of its signatories lists his name with the notation that the signature has been erased.
suggested_refs: The 1993 Constitution of Peru and its catalogue of signatories

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the title passes to the daughter
stops.date_confidence: [R] for the month: the dossier places the removal in August 1994 and it was not confirmed against a contemporaneous news account in this pass. Keiko was nineteen, born 25 May 1975 [A, en.wikipedia]. The divorce was formalised by a Lima tribunal in 1995; 1994 is the separation and removal year. Coordinate is the canonical Casa de Pizarro pin.
stops.campa: Susana Higuchi tells the press that his relatives have been selling clothing donated from Japan for the poor. She is answered from inside the same house. The office of First Lady is taken from her and given to Keiko, nineteen years old and reading business administration abroad. No article of the constitution creates the office, so no article governs its transfer either. Keiko presides at state dinners from that year, and her mother begins a political career against her father. A Lima tribunal formalises the divorce in 1995.
suggested_refs: Susana Higuchi's public statements of 1994 on the Japanese aid donations
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, 'Palacio de Gobierno, the title passes to the daughter'

stops.name: Cenepa valley, the war in the cordillera
stops.date_confidence: [R] for the war's detail, dossier synthesis not independently fetched; the reelection at about 64.4 per cent against Javier Perez de Cuellar in April 1995 is [A] from en.wikipedia. Coordinate approximates the disputed border sector. Government claims about control of Tiwinza were disputed at the time and are not adopted here.
stops.campa: Peru and Ecuador fight for a month over an undemarcated stretch of the Cordillera del Condor, jungle so steep that helicopters cannot put down in it. He flies to the front repeatedly in fatigues and is photographed there, and the photographs run in every newspaper in Peru. Neither army takes the valley outright, and the government's claims about holding Tiwinza are contested while the shooting is still going on. The border question itself stays open until 1998. In April, ten weeks after the firing stops, he is reelected with about sixty-four per cent against Javier Perez de Cuellar.
suggested_refs: The Cenepa War of January-February 1995 and the disputed Tiwinza communiques

stops.name: San Isidro, the residence taken
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia, 'Japanese embassy hostage crisis', gives 17 December 1996, fourteen MRTA under Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, and a reception for Emperor Akihito's birthday. The headcount is corrected: over 600 guests initially, reduced to about 381 men and then to 72. The dossier's 'roughly 800' is not carried. Coordinate reconciled to the Wikipedia and Nominatim position on Calle Tomas Edison, matching the afterlife lens.
stops.campa: Fourteen members of the Tupac Amaru movement come through the wall of the Japanese ambassador's residence on Calle Tomas Edison during a reception for the birthday of Emperor Akihito. More than six hundred guests are inside: ministers, judges, generals and much of the diplomatic corps of Lima. Over the following weeks the captors release most of them and keep seventy-two men. The siege runs a hundred and twenty-six days. He refuses to negotiate anything of substance and has a tunnel dug under the house.
suggested_refs: The Japanese ambassador's residence at Calle Tomas Edison 210, San Isidro

stops.name: San Isidro, Chavin de Huantar
stops.date_confidence: attested for the raid, the casualties and the date. The quotation is [A] verbatim, but it is a 2017 written statement, not a 1997 remark: a handwritten letter released on 20 April 2017 through Kenji Fujimori's Twitter account for the twentieth anniversary, reproduced by La Vanguardia (EFE) and RPP. The allegation that some captors were shot after surrendering is contested; the Inter-American Court substantiated it for one victim, Cruz Sanchez, without any criminal conviction of Fujimori.
stops.campa: At twenty past three in the afternoon the floor of the house opens and a hundred and forty commandos come up out of the tunnels while charges blow the roof. It takes sixteen minutes. All fourteen captors die; one hostage dies, the supreme court justice Carlos Giusti; two commandos die; seventy-one of the seventy-two come out alive. A defence intelligence cable and forensic testimony will later allege that some of the captors were shot after surrendering, and the Inter-American Court will substantiate that for one of them.
stops.quote: Cuando analizaba opciones distintas a la salida pacifica, los admirables tuneles de Chavin felizmente vinieron en un sueno que inspiro el rescate.
stops.quote_source: Alberto Fujimori, handwritten letter from prison released 20 April 2017 through Kenji Fujimori's Twitter account for the twentieth anniversary of the rescue; reproduced verbatim by La Vanguardia (EFE) and RPP the same day. Accents removed here to keep the file in plain ASCII
suggested_refs: Inter-American Court of Human Rights, Cruz Sanchez et al. v. Peru (2015)

stops.name: Jesus Maria, the nationality taken from Baruch Ivcher
stops.date_confidence: attested in the dossier (line 155) for 1997; no day or month is given in the sources reached, so the month here is a placeholder. The Inter-American Court's finding of Peruvian responsibility is [A]. Coordinate is the dossier's Frecuencia Latina studio pin in Jesus Maria and was not independently re-verified.
stops.campa: Baruch Ivcher Bronstein, an Israeli-born businessman naturalised Peruvian, owns the channel that broadcasts the torture of the intelligence agent Leonor La Rosa and the account of the intelligence service's telephone interceptions. The state answers by annulling his naturalisation, which under Peruvian law removes his right to own a broadcaster, and control of the station passes to minority shareholders who change its line. He leaves the country. In 2001 the Inter-American Court finds Peru responsible for the annulment.
suggested_refs: The Leonor La Rosa broadcasts of April 1997 on Frecuencia Latina
sources: Inter-American Court of Human Rights, Ivcher Bronstein v. Peru (2001)

stops.name: Itamaraty, the Brasilia Presidential Act
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia, 'Cenepa War', confirms the Brasilia Presidential Act of 26 October 1998 with the four guarantor states present. Coordinate corrected to the Nominatim position of the Palacio Itamaraty; the dossier's pin fell about 3.2 km away. The Tiwinza property arrangement of 1999 and the APEC accession dates are [R], dossier synthesis.
stops.campa: At the Itamaraty Palace he and Jamil Mahuad of Ecuador sign the Brasilia Presidential Act in front of the four guarantor states, closing a border question left open since 1942 and fought over three years before. Markers go into the Cordillera del Condor the following year, and Ecuador receives a square kilometre at Tiwinza as private property while the sovereignty over it stays Peruvian. Peru enters APEC across the same seasons, from the Vancouver decision of 1997 to the Kuala Lumpur summit of 1998.
suggested_refs: The Brasilia Presidential Act, 26 October 1998, and the 1999 demarcation of the Cordillera del Condor

segments.name: The Third Term and the Tape

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the third oath and the Marcha de los Cuatro Suyos
stops.date_confidence: attested for the oath of 28 July 2000 and for the Banco de la Nacion fire in which six security guards died; responsibility for the fire was never judicially established against Fujimori. The third-term election of 28 May 2000 and the Carter Center findings are [R], dossier synthesis, not independently fetched. Coordinate is the canonical Casa de Pizarro pin.
stops.campa: He is declared the winner of a third term after an election that the Carter Center and other monitors document as fraudulent, and after his runoff opponent Alejandro Toledo withdraws rather than legitimise it. On the day of the oath, four columns of marchers walk into the centre of Lima from four directions, named for the four suyos of the Inca division of the world. Smoke goes up over the centre of the city. Six security guards die in a fire at the Banco de la Nacion, and no court has ever established who set it.
suggested_refs: Carter Center and OAS observation reports on the Peruvian general election of 2000
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, 'Palacio de Justicia, the Marcha de los Cuatro Suyos'

stops.name: Plaza San Martin, the tape at the Hotel Bolivar
stops.date_confidence: [R] for the detail of the screening, dossier synthesis not independently fetched in this pass; the date, the sum and the two names are consistent across the dossier and the already-researched files of Susana Higuchi and Keiko Fujimori. Coordinate inherited byte-for-byte from susana_higuchi.journey.json.
stops.campa: In a room at the Gran Hotel Bolivar on the Plaza San Martin, opposition politicians play a videotape to the press. On it Vladimiro Montesinos, the intelligence adviser who holds no office anyone can name, counts fifteen thousand dollars into the hands of a newly elected opposition congressman, Alberto Kouri, in exchange for his defection to the government bench. Canal N broadcasts it. Thousands more tapes exist, filmed by Montesinos in his own office, of judges, editors, generals and businessmen taking money.
suggested_refs: The vladivideo archive seized in 2000-2001 and used in the subsequent prosecutions
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, 'Plaza San Martin, the first vladivideo at the Hotel Bolivar'

stops.name: Lima, the message of the sixteenth of September
stops.date_confidence: attested: the address is preserved in full at es.wikisource, 'Mensaje a la Nacion de Alberto Fujimori, 16 de septiembre de 2000', where both quoted sentences appear verbatim. The dossier and es.wikiquote date these lines only to 'c. 2000' via a secondary reprint; the wikisource primary settles both date and occasion. Coordinate is a general-Lima pin for a national broadcast.
stops.campa: Two days after the tape he goes on national television. He deactivates the intelligence service, calls new general elections, and announces that he will not be a candidate in them. He does not resign. He says that his two terms of government have not been free of errors or omissions, which is as close to an admission as the record holds, and he asks the country to remember what he takes to be the achievements. There are four months of his presidency left.
stops.quote: He gobernado el Peru diez anos. Ni los detractores pueden dejar de reconocer logros fundamentales que no los enumerare, ustedes los conocen.
stops.quote_source: Alberto Fujimori, Mensaje a la Nacion, Lima, 16 September 2000, es.wikisource. Accents removed here to keep the file in plain ASCII; the same address carries the sentence 'Mis dos periodos de Gobierno, lo reconozco, no estan exentos de errores u omisiones'
suggested_refs: The full text of the Mensaje a la Nacion of 16 September 2000
sources: es.wikisource, 'Mensaje a la Nacion de Alberto Fujimori, 16 de septiembre de 2000'
es.wikiquote, 'Alberto Fujimori', citing Gustavo Johnson (2001) pp. 6-7 and p. 498

stops.name: Lima, the aircraft on the runway
stops.date_confidence: [R] tradition, and flagged as such in paul_singer.journey.json, which carries the same episode at the same coordinate. No filing, no date and no airfield has ever been produced for it. November 2000 is placed to match the flight itself, not because any source dates the episode.
stops.campa: A story attaches itself to the collapse and has never been dislodged from it: that Elliott Management, holding fifty-eight million dollars of defaulted Peruvian paper bought at a discount, had his aircraft confiscated in Lima and offered him passage in exchange for the treasury settling. The debt is real and was settled. The aircraft is another matter. In a quarter of a century nobody has produced a filing, a date or the name of an airfield, and Paul Singer has never publicly denied any of it either.
suggested_refs: Elliott Associates v. Republic of Peru and the 2000 settlement of the defaulted Peruvian paper

stops.name: Bandar Seri Begawan, the last summit
stops.date_confidence: attested in the dossier (line 163) for the departure to the APEC summit at Brunei on 13 November 2000; en.wikipedia confirms that he travelled from Brunei to Tokyo on 17 November.
stops.campa: He flies to the APEC summit at Bandar Seri Begawan on the thirteenth of November, the last official journey of a Peruvian president who is, on paper, still in office. Congress has already begun the motion to declare the presidency vacant. He does not go home. From Brunei he continues to Tokyo, a city he has visited many times as a head of state, and where his parents' nationality has been waiting quietly for him for sixty-two years. The delegation that travelled out with him returns to Lima without him.
suggested_refs: The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Bandar Seri Begawan, November 2000

stops.name: Tokyo, the resignation by fax
stops.date_confidence: contested date. en.wikipedia's sentence dates 17 November to the Brunei-to-Tokyo flight and does not separately date the fax; the dossier gives 20 November; the commonly cited date is 19 November. Congress rejected the resignation on 21 November. The fax therefore falls between 17 and 21 November 2000 and the day is not fixed here. Coordinate inherited byte-for-byte from keiko_fujimori.journey.json.
stops.campa: From a hotel in Tokyo he sends the Congress of Peru a facsimile resigning the presidency of the republic. The exact day is not fixed in the record: it falls between the seventeenth, when he lands from Brunei, and the twenty-first, when Congress refuses to accept the document. Refusing it is deliberate. A resignation would leave him a former president who stepped down; a vacancy declared for moral incapacity leaves him a president who was removed. Peru litigates the difference for the next ten years.
stops.quote: Formulo, pues, ante usted, senor presidente del Congreso, mi renuncia formal a la Presidencia de la Republica...
stops.quote_source: Resignation faxed from Tokyo to the Congress of Peru, November 2000, as compiled in es.wikiquote citing Gustavo Johnson (2001) p. 84; the underlying book page was not reachable in this pass. Accents removed here to keep the file in plain ASCII
suggested_refs: The text of the resignation faxed to the Congress of Peru, November 2000
sources: es.wikiquote, 'Alberto Fujimori', citing Gustavo Johnson (2001) p. 84
keiko_fujimori.journey.json, 'Tokyo, the father who resigned by fax'

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, permanent moral incapacity
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives the congressional vote of 22 November 2000 to remove him; the tally of 62-9 with nine abstentions is from the dossier. es.wikipedia's list of Peruvian presidents ends his mandate on 21 November, the day the resignation was refused, so the two dates mark two different acts. Coordinate is the canonical Palacio Legislativo pin.
stops.campa: Congress declares the presidency vacant by sixty-two votes to nine with nine abstentions, on the ground of permanent moral incapacity, a formula written into Peruvian constitutions since the nineteenth century and never once defined by any of them. The chamber he emptied with soldiers eight years earlier empties his office by a show of hands. Valentin Paniagua, president of the Congress, takes the sash. The transitional government begins the work of counting the tapes.
suggested_refs: The congressional resolution of 22 November 2000 declaring the presidency vacant
sources: susana_higuchi.journey.json, 'Congreso de la Republica, the censure and Valentin Paniagua'

stops.name: Tokyo, the nationality that could not be extradited
stops.date_confidence: [R] for the 12 December 2000 date of the Foreign Ministry finding, dossier synthesis not independently fetched; the substance, that Japan recognised his nationality on the basis of the 1938 consular registration and does not extradite its nationals, is corroborated by en.wikipedia. The exile years to 2005 and the Si Cumple organising are [R], dossier lines 165-169. No fixed Tokyo residence address was located.
stops.campa: In December the Japanese Foreign Ministry announces that Alberto Fujimori holds Japanese nationality, because his parents registered his birth with their consulate in Lima in 1938, and that Japan does not extradite its own nationals. The finding also disposes of the old accusation that he was born in Kumamoto on a forged Peruvian record, since a birth in Japan would have needed no consular registration at all. He stays five years, lectures, writes in the language he learned before Spanish, and organises a movement to carry him home.
suggested_refs: The Japanese Foreign Ministry nationality determination of December 2000

stops.name: Santiago, ten hours after the private jet
stops.date_confidence: contested date. es.wikipedia, 'Juicio a Alberto Fujimori', gives arrival by private jet as a tourist, a room at the Hotel Marriott, and arrest about ten hours later on 6 November 2005; much of the contemporary press dates the arrest to the early hours of 7 November. en.wikipedia gives only 'November 2005', and the dossier's attribution of a 5 November date to Wikipedia is false and is not carried here.
stops.campa: He lands at Santiago in a private jet, entering Chile as a tourist, and takes a room at the Marriott. He means to be one border away from Peru when the 2006 campaign opens. Chilean police arrest him about ten hours later on Peru's extradition request, though much of the press dates the arrest to the small hours of the following day. He had left Japan, the one jurisdiction on earth that could not send him back, of his own accord and under no obligation whatever. The next twenty-three months go to Chilean custody and Chilean courts.
suggested_refs: Chilean extradition file on Alberto Fujimori, 2005-2007

stops.name: Las Condes, bail and a second marriage
stops.date_confidence: attested in the dossier (lines 173-175) for release to bail on 18 May 2006 after six months in custody and for the registration of a marriage to Satomi Kataoka on 6 April 2006; not independently re-fetched in this pass. Keiko's 2006 congressional election with the largest personal vote in the country is from keiko_fujimori.journey.json.
stops.campa: After six months in custody he is released to bail in a rented house in Las Condes, in the eastern hills above Santiago, under an order not to leave the country. He registers a marriage there in April 2006 to Satomi Kataoka, a Japanese hotelier. From the same house he watches his daughter Keiko take a seat in the Peruvian congress on the largest personal vote in the country. He also stands for the Japanese upper house that year, from Chilean house arrest, and loses.
suggested_refs: Chilean bail order of 18 May 2006 and the Kataoka marriage registration of 6 April 2006

stops.name: Santiago, the Supreme Court of Chile
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia records the September 2007 extradition; the dossier (line 177) supplies the tally of seven of thirteen counts and their subject matter. Coordinate approximates the court's Santiago location.
stops.campa: The Supreme Court of Chile authorises extradition on seven of the thirteen counts Peru asked for: Barrios Altos, La Cantuta, the kidnappings of the journalist Gustavo Gorriti and the businessman Samuel Dyer, and several of the corruption files. It is the first time any court has extradited a former head of state to his own country to stand trial for human-rights crimes. He is flown to Lima the same day, and the aircraft is met by an escort that takes him straight east, out of the city, into a police compound at Ate.
suggested_refs: Corte Suprema de Chile, extradition ruling of 21 September 2007

stops.name: Barbadillo, into the police compound
stops.date_confidence: attested for the confinement from 22 September 2007. The quotation's date is corrected: RPP's retrospective is published 4 July 2017, but the words were spoken on 10 December 2007 at the opening hearing before the Sala Penal Especial sitting at the DIROES base, when the presiding judge Cesar San Martin gave him the floor; corroborated by El Correo's contemporaneous dispatch. The elided middle sentence is restored. Coordinate inherited byte-for-byte from keiko_fujimori.journey.json.
stops.campa: Barbadillo is a small building inside the police special-operations compound at Ate, built to hold one prisoner. He has a bed, a desk, a garden and long family visits, and his supporters call it the unjust confinement of a sick old man while his opponents call it a golden prison. The human-rights trial opens on the base itself, in a courtroom fitted up for it, before the Sala Penal Especial on the tenth of December. Given the floor by the presiding judge, Cesar San Martin, he condemns what was done and denies having ordered it.
stops.quote: Si se cometieron hechos execrables los condeno, pero no fueron ordenes de quien habla. Por eso senor presidente rechazo los cargos totalmente. Soy inocente!
stops.quote_source: Alberto Fujimori at the opening hearing of his human-rights trial, Sala Penal Especial, DIROES base, Ate, 10 December 2007, as reported by RPP and by El Correo. Accents and the opening inverted exclamation removed here to keep the file in plain ASCII
suggested_refs: The trial record of the Sala Penal Especial, DIROES base, Ate, 2007-2009
sources: RPP, 'El dia en que Alberto Fujimori grito Soy inocente' (Jose Flores)
OpenStreetMap/Nominatim, Penal de Barbadillo, Vitarte, Ate

stops.name: Barbadillo, twenty-five years
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives the human-rights conviction of 7 April 2009 and a 25-year sentence, the embezzlement conviction of 20 July 2009 with seven and a half years, and the bribery and media-purchase conviction of 30 September 2009 with six years. The three 2009 verdicts are gathered into one stop here; they were handed down at the same site.
stops.campa: After fifteen months of hearings the court convicts him as the indirect perpetrator of the Barrios Altos and La Cantuta killings and of the Gorriti and Dyer kidnappings, and sentences him to twenty-five years. The doctrine it applies is that a man at the top of an organised apparatus of power is the author of what the apparatus does, whether or not he gave any particular order for it. Two further convictions follow in the same year: fifteen million dollars of state money moved to Montesinos, and a television channel's editorial line bought outright.
suggested_refs: Sentencia de la Sala Penal Especial de la Corte Suprema, Exp. AV 19-2001, 7 April 2009

stops.name: Barbadillo, the pardon of Christmas Eve
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives the humanitarian pardon granted by President Pedro Pablo Kuczynski on 24 December 2017 on health grounds, days after a bloc led by Kenji Fujimori withheld the impeachment votes that saved Kuczynski's presidency. The causal link between the two is asserted in every account and was never established by any court.
stops.campa: On Christmas Eve, President Pedro Pablo Kuczynski signs a humanitarian pardon on grounds of his health. Three days earlier a bloc of congressmen led by his son Kenji had withheld the votes that would have removed Kuczynski from office. The two facts are set side by side in every account written since and were never joined by any court. He leaves the compound for a clinic. Crowds gather outside it with flags, and a different set of crowds gathers in the Plaza San Martin holding photographs of the dead of La Cantuta.
suggested_refs: Resolucion Suprema 281-2017-JUS granting the humanitarian pardon

stops.name: Barbadillo, the pardon undone
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives the Supreme Court's reversal of the pardon on 3 October 2018 for lack of necessity, proportionality and adequate medical foundation, and his return to prison. The quotation is compiled in es.wikiquote from an America Noticias report of 2018; the original page returned 404 and only the compilation was reachable.
stops.campa: The Supreme Court annuls the pardon: not necessary, not proportionate, not medically founded. The ruling is handed down on the third of October 2018, nine months after he left the compound for a clinic. He goes back inside in January, eighty years old, carried in and out of clinics on a stretcher. The pardon becomes the single standing question in Peruvian politics, argued in the courts, in Congress and before the Inter-American Court, which holds that a state cannot pardon its way out of a judgment it has been ordered to enforce.
stops.quote: Por favor, no me usen como arma politica porque ya no tengo fuerzas para resistirlo.
stops.quote_source: Alberto Fujimori, statement reported by America Noticias in 2018 during the fight over the annulment of his pardon, as compiled in es.wikiquote; the original page was not reachable. Accents removed here to keep the file in plain ASCII
suggested_refs: Inter-American Court of Human Rights, supervision-of-compliance orders in Barrios Altos and La Cantuta v. Peru

stops.name: Barbadillo, the book written in the cell
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia, 'La palabra del chino', confirms that the first volume, el intruso, was written at the Penal de Barbadillo with Victor Paredes and Ricardo Rivera and published in 2021, and that the second, el inconforme, written during his post-pardon liberty, was presented posthumously in Iquitos by Keiko Fujimori. The article gives no ISBN and no 2022 registration date, so the dossier's ISBN detail is dropped; it gives 2025 without a month. The claim of further unreleased manuscripts is [R], a family statement relayed through the same article. The month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: In the cell he writes, with Victor Paredes and Ricardo Rivera, a memoir he titles La palabra del chino, taking up the nickname the country gave him in the first campaign for a man whose parents came from Japan and not from China. The first volume, el intruso, appears in 2021. A second, el inconforme, is written during his brief liberty after the pardon and is not presented in public until after his death, in Iquitos, by Keiko. The family says further manuscripts were left ready.
suggested_refs: La palabra del chino: el intruso (2021) and el inconforme (presented Iquitos, 2025)

stops.name: Barbadillo, the walk out
stops.date_confidence: attested and the apparent discrepancy resolved: en.wikipedia gives 5 December 2023 for the order of immediate release and the following day for the walk-out itself, after sixteen years inside. The Constitutional Court had reinstated the 2017 pardon by four votes to three on 17 March 2022. Coordinate inherited byte-for-byte from keiko_fujimori.journey.json.
stops.campa: The Constitutional Court restores the pardon by four votes to three in March 2022 and, on the fifth of December 2023, orders the ruling carried out at once. The Inter-American Court had ordered Peru not to release him, and Peru releases him anyway; the state that convicted him and the court supervising the conviction have not agreed about it since. He walks out of Barbadillo the next day, after sixteen years inside, into a car with Keiko and Kenji. He is eighty-five.
suggested_refs: Peruvian Constitutional Court ruling of 17 March 2022 and the execution order of 5 December 2023

stops.name: San Borja, the house of the daughter
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives death on 11 September 2024 at Keiko Fujimori's home in San Borja from complications of recurrent tongue cancer. The Pativilca case was still in hearings at his death and produced no verdict against him. Coordinate is the dossier's San Borja residence pin, approximate at street level.
stops.campa: He lives out his last nine months in his daughter's house in San Borja, under treatment for a tongue cancer that had been cut out once and came back. He dies there on the eleventh of September 2024, at eighty-six, with his children in the house. The government of Dina Boluarte declares three days of national mourning for a man its own courts had convicted. Of the cases against him, one conviction had been pardoned, the rest stood, and the Pativilca hearings were still running on the day he died.
suggested_refs: Peruvian government decree of national mourning, September 2024

stops.name: San Borja, the museum and the theatre
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia records the lying-in-state at the Museo de la Nacion from 12 to 14 September 2024 and the state funeral at the National Theatre on 14 September, with President Boluarte's salute and Keiko Fujimori speaking. Coordinate corrected to the Nominatim position of the Museo de la Nacion, Avenida Javier Prado Este 2300, matching the afterlife lens; the Gran Teatro Nacional stands one block away at -12.0866, -77.0032 and is folded into this stop.
stops.campa: His body lies in state for three days at the Museo de la Nacion on Avenida Javier Prado, the culture ministry's building in San Borja, with the honours given to a serving head of state. On the fourteenth the state funeral is held one block away at the Gran Teatro Nacional, where President Boluarte salutes the coffin and Keiko speaks in front of a portrait of her father the height of the stage. He was, on the day of that ceremony, a convicted man. The state buried him as a president.
suggested_refs: The Museo de la Nacion and the Gran Teatro Nacional, San Borja, September 2024

stops.name: Huachipa, the Cementerio Campo Fe
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives burial at Campo Fe cemetery, Huachipa, on 14 September 2024. Coordinate inherited byte-for-byte from susana_higuchi.journey.json, where she was buried in 2021; that the two graves are in the same cemetery is [A] for the cemetery, not verified as to plot. The El Ojo que Llora vandalism of 23 September 2007 and the 2015 opening of the Lugar de la Memoria are [A] from en.wikipedia and are cited here as afterlife, not staged as stops of his own.
stops.campa: He is buried at the Campo Fe cemetery at Huachipa, upriver from Lima on the Rimac, in the same ground that took Susana Higuchi three years before him. Outside the gate the argument does not close. The Lugar de la Memoria in Miraflores holds the whole Fujimori decade inside a building designed to house disagreement rather than settle it, and the memorial at the Campo de Marte still carries the stones that his sympathisers splashed with orange paint, his campaign colour, the day after he was extradited.
suggested_refs: El Ojo que Llora, Campo de Marte, Jesus Maria, vandalised 23 September 2007
Lugar de la Memoria, la Tolerancia y la Inclusion Social, Miraflores, opened 2015
sources: en.wikipedia, 'Place of Memory, Tolerance and Social Inclusion'
